accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorems 1–3 / honest_scope
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Outcome and covariate smoothness are known for the oracle pilot and projection resolutions; the observable upper frontier is asserted only when the displayed pilot-feasibility inequality holds.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The expansion and matched conditional minimax rate are conditional on the stated known-smoothness, positive anisotropic-density model and its pilot-feasible regime; outside it only the explicit lower bound is claimed.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 2 / honest_scope
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: A fixed Gaussian-chaos limit is not claimed without convergence of the normalized spectral and local-shift arrays.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The primary conclusion is the stated triangular Gaussian-quadratic approximation; fixed chaos is conditional on the explicit subsequential ℓ² convergence condition.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 4 / honest_scope
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The no-covariate result uses a separate full-sample empirical-quantile construction rather than the conditional split-sample tuning.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The d=0 recovery and exact null constant apply to the declared separate branch only.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2506.00257v2, 12 February 2026; cited AISTATS 2026 proceedings primary was access-blocked at OpenReview
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The accessible author version proposes a direct consistent nonparametric COT-value estimator and derives a convergence rate. No proceedings theorem-level formula comparison was made because the primary text was inaccessible.
The journal article studies distributional limits for weighted L2 empirical-quantile-process functionals, including weighted Wasserstein statistics.

It establishes first-order differentiability generally and second-order differentiability at the equal-counterfactual-distribution null for a fixed-entropic Sinkhorn treatment effect, with debiased inference.

source_verification_receipts.version: Stochastic Processes and their Applications 126(12), 2016, pp. 3733–3759
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves conditional asymptotic normality for changing-kernel quadratic U-statistics dominated by their degenerate second-order component.
The paper develops second-order inference for functionals with null first derivative, identifies ordinary-bootstrap failure, and gives derivative-aware bootstrap corrections.
The article gives minimax Wasserstein-density-estimation rates over smooth densities, using negative-order/Besov geometry and distinguishing lower-bounded densities.
The article proves sharp unconditional empirical-OT convergence rates for smooth costs, including separation-sensitive improvements and lower bounds.
